plan.english: Be well, shepherd! Where does this path go? It goes over the hill to the settlement. Whose son are you? I am the son of Of-Good-Horses. I am seeking my brother. A young man came here yesterday. He went toward the river. Is the river far? It is not far. Follow the path, and at evening you will see the river. May the gods guard you.

plan.english: Husband, this night I saw an evil dream. You were lying on the way, and you were not alive. Dreams deceive. Grasp my hand: I am alive. Do not go to the far settlement! The clan chief wants me. I will go, and I will come back unharmed. When will you return home? I will return home with the first snow. May the gods protect you, and I will wait for you.

plan.english: Guest, you have walked on long ways: tell us a tale. Toward the dawn, on the wide earth, a people lives on wagons. They have no villages. They drink the milk of their own herds and eat flesh. Are they friendly to guests? They were friendly to me: their chief gave me a foal. Where is that foal now? It stands in your pasture: now it has grown big.

plan.english: Wife, I have come! Did the sheep stay alive in the winter? They stayed alive: the winter was cold, and the cow-stall was warm. Five lambs were born in the spring. Is our daughter well? She has grown up, and now she weaves wool. And what are you bringing us? For you I bring a knife of copper, and for our daughter a red garment. You are dear to us: sit down and eat.

I am alone; the road is my friend. Will you tell us a tale? Sit down, children, and listen. An eagle was carrying a shepherd over the high mountains.

Take this spear: may it protect you on the way. And you, take my knife. May the gods give you swift feet! And may your load be small! Be well, friend!

plan.english: Old man, I will go toward the sinking sun. Why will you go? No one has come home unharmed from that way. I seek the end of the earth, and I will win great fame. When my beard was black, I too was seeking fame. I found a wife and a hearth. That is better than fame. You are wise; I am young. Grandson, may you come home unharmed!

plan.english: Of-Goodly-Fame, how did your boat break? Listen! We were rowing on the sea, and Perkwunos thundered. The wind broke it, and the men sank. Then how did you get free? I seized timber and swam to the land. Now I do not row: I shepherd sheep. Do you fear Perkwunos? I do not fear him: I praise him.

The earth was dry, and the grain did not grow. Will the new earth be good? Its streams are many, and its grass is high. Then I will be glad. Sleep now: the wagon rocks you.

I will put meat into the cauldron and warm the mead. May he be bringing me a gift! You think of gifts; I think of him.
